title: What can you say about fenugreek in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 5 wordings for fenugreek; the strongest is "A source of antioxidants that help protect cells against damage from free radicals" (limited, up to 30 g dried seed (or extract equivalent) a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Lowers blood sugar in diabetes, or helps manage diabetes".

supported_wordings.wording: A source of antioxidants that help protect cells against damage from free radicals.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it with a maximum dose only and no minimum; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: up to 30 g dried seed (or extract equivalent) a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older, up to 30 g a day. Health Canada sets no minimum for this use.
supported_wordings.form: Dried seed or non-standardized seed extracts

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers blood sugar in diabetes, or helps manage diabetes
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. Health Canada's wording is about supporting healthy glucose levels, with a caution for people with diabetes.
Names a disease. Health Canada lists this herbal use, but it names a disease.
Names diseases. Health Canada lists this herbal use, but it names diseases.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Boosts testosterone, or treats low testosterone
wordings_to_avoid.why: Low testosterone as a diagnosis is a medical condition; no listed source supports a testosterone claim for fenugreek.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
